question: What is a 'Stock Item' in Indian Railways and Metro Railway store management?

options.A: An item required for a one-time project only
options.B: An item for which a regular stock is maintained in Stores Depots due to frequent and recurring demand
options.C: An item purchased directly from local retail market by the user shop
options.D: An item that cannot be coded with a PL number

question: What is a 'Non-Stock Item'?

options.A: An item stored permanently in huge quantities in depot wards
options.B: An item needed for a specific work/sanctioned estimate, non-recurring in nature, and not kept in regular store inventory
options.C: An item that has zero purchase cost
options.D: An item issued only to administrative officers

question: How many digits are standardly used in an Indian Railway Price Ledger (PL) Number for identifying stock items?

options.A: 6 digits

question: In an 8-digit PL Number '30 12 345 6', what do the first two digits '30' represent?

options.A: Sub-group of the item
options.B: Main Group / Category of the store item

question: In an 8-digit PL Number, what do the 3rd and 4th digits represent?

options.A: Main Group

question: What is the purpose of the 8th (last) digit in a PL Number?

options.A: It indicates the price of the item
options.B: It is a Check Digit calculated using a computer algorithm to prevent data entry errors
options.C: It indicates the shelf life in months

question: Which Railway Stores Form is standardly used by the user shop as a Requisition / Issue Note (S-1313) to draw Stock Items from Stores Depot?

options.A: Form S-1302

question: Which form is used by an indented shop/office for Requisitioning Non-Stock Items?

options.A: Form S-1302 (Indent for Non-Stock Items)

question: Which online portal is used across Indian Railways and Metro Railway for e-procurement and digital indenting of non-stock materials?

options.A: IREPS (Indian Railways E-Procurement System) / iMMIS

question: What does iMMIS stand for in Railway Store Management?

options.A: Integrated Material Management Information System

question: What is 'ABC Analysis' in inventory management of Railway stores?

options.A: Categorization of store items based on their annual consumption value
options.B: Classification based on weight of items

question: In ABC Analysis, 'A' Category items represent approximately what proportion of total store inventory value?

options.A: 70% to 80% of total annual consumption value (covering ~10-15% of total items)

question: In ABC Analysis, 'C' Category items represent:

options.A: High-value items
options.B: Low-value items representing ~65-70% of total inventory items but only ~5-10% of total consumption value

question: What does 'VED Analysis' stand for in railway store classification?

options.A: Volume, Energy, Weight Analysis

question: In VED Analysis, 'Vital' (V) items are those whose non-availability results in:

options.A: Immediate total breakdown or stoppage of train operations / maintenance work

question: What is 'FSN Analysis' in stores management?

options.A: Fast moving, Slow moving, and Non-moving (Dead) stock classification

question: What is 'Dead Stock' or 'Surplus Stock'?

options.A: Items for which there has been no demand/issue for 24 months or more

question: What is a 'Proprietary Article Certificate' (PAC)?

options.A: Certificate issued by the indenting officer confirming that a specific brand/make is required and no other substitute is acceptable

question: PAC Indenting under Model Schedule of Powers (Model SOP) Form 16(a) is submitted when:

options.A: The required item is manufactured only by a single specific firm and no substitute available
options.B: Item is manufactured by thousands of local suppliers

question: Who must approve a PAC Non-Stock Indent of high value as per Railway Model SOP before submission to Stores?

options.A: Competent Technical Officer (e.g., SAG officer / DRM / CWM / HOD depending on financial threshold)

question: What is 'Accounts Vetting' of a Non-Stock Indent?

options.A: Financial scrutiny and endorsement of the indent by the Associate Finance/Accounts officer prior to procurement

question: Is Accounts Vetting required for ALL non-stock indents regardless of value?

options.A: Yes, always required
options.B: No, threshold financial limits are fixed under SOP below which indents can be processed directly without prior vetting

question: What is the primary document used to return unserviceable scrap or excess raw material from user shop back to Stores Depot?

options.A: Advice Note of Returned Stores (Form S-1539)

question: How many copies of Advice Note of Returned Stores (Form S-1539) are generally prepared by the returning shop?

options.A: 2 copies
options.B: 6 copies (or as prescribed for accountal, ward receipt, and user acknowledgment)

question: When raw material already drawn for Work Order 'X' is transferred to Work Order 'Y' within the shop, which form must be processed?

options.A: Advice of Material Transfer (Form S-1727)

question: What is 'Stocking Proposal' in store management?

options.A: Proposal submitted by user department to convert a frequently used Non-Stock item into a regular Stock Item
options.B: Proposal to sell all store items
options.C: Proposal to build new staff quarters
options.D: Proposal to close the stores depot

question: A Stocking Proposal must contain which of the following essential details?

options.A: Anticipated annual consumption, estimated rate, specification, recommended initial stock level, and justification

question: Who gives the final financial and technical sanction for converting a Non-Stock item to a Stock Item?

options.A: Principal Chief Material Manager (PCMM) / Competent Stores & Finance Authority

question: What is 'Lead Time' in stores procurement?

options.A: Time spent in loading material
options.B: Total time elapsed between initiation of indent/requisition and actual physical receipt of material in depot
options.C: Time spent in worker lunch break
options.D: Time taken by train to reach station

question: What is 'Buffer Stock' (Safety Stock)?

options.A: Extra reserve inventory maintained to protect against sudden spikes in demand or delays in supply during lead time

question: What is 'Re-Order Level' (ROL)?

options.A: Stock level at which an automated fresh procurement action/indent must be triggered to replenish stock before depletion

question: Formula for Re-Order Level (ROL) is generally expressed as:

options.A: ROL = (Minimum Stock / Safety Stock) + Lead Time Consumption

question: What is 'Maximum Stock Level'?

options.A: Upper limit of stock inventory above which holding stock causes unnecessary working capital blockage and holding cost

question: What is 'Minimum Stock Level'?

options.A: Stock level below which inventory should not normally fall; acts as safety margin before buffer stock is tapped
options.B: Highest amount of stock in store

question: What is 'Imprest Stores' in workshop/maintenance depot management?

options.A: Fixed standing quantity of specific recurring maintenance materials held directly by the user shop SSE for immediate day-to-day work

question: How are Imprest Stores replenished (recouped) when consumed?

options.A: User SSE submits an Imprest Recoupment Requisition (Form S-1830 / S-1313) to Stores Depot to bring stock back to sanctioned limit
options.B: By purchasing from open market without permission

question: How often are Imprest Store limits reviewed jointly by User Department and Stores/Finance?

options.A: Periodically (typically once a year or every two years) to adjust limits based on actual consumption patterns

question: What is 'Emergency Purchase' of non-stock items?

options.A: Special purchase powers exercised by officers to procure critical items urgently to avoid operational breakdown
options.B: Purchase made during night shift without bill

question: Under GeM (Government e-Marketplace), common use goods and services are procured as per Government mandate. What does GeM stand for?

options.A: General Electrical Machinery

question: Under current Railway directives, procurement of common-use store goods available on GeM portal is:

options.A: Mandatory through GeM portal beyond prescribed financial limits

question: What is a 'Consignee' in store procurement documentation?

options.A: The official user/depot receiving authority to whom the purchased goods are to be delivered

question: What is 'Inspection Authority' in store purchase orders?

options.A: Designated agency (e.g., RITES, RDSO, or Consignee) responsible for inspecting and certifying material quality before dispatch

question: What does RITES stand for in railway material inspection Context?

options.A: Rail India Technical and Economic Service
options.B: Railway Industrial Testing and Electrical Standards

question: What does RDSO stand for?

options.A: Research Designs and Standards Organisation

question: When material is inspected by Consignee directly at destination upon receipt, it is called:

options.A: Consignee Inspection

question: What document is generated by Stores Depot when incoming stock material is physically received and accepted into ward balance?

options.A: Receipt Note / Stores Receipt Sheet (Form S-1307)

question: What is 'Rejection Advice' (Rejection Memo) issued by Stores Depot / Consignee?

options.A: Formal notification sent to vendor and accounts rejecting supplied material due to defects/non-conformance to drawing
options.B: Approval letter to pay vendor bill

question: Within how many days should rejected non-conforming material generally be lifted by the vendor from railway premises after rejection advice?

options.A: 21 days (or as specified in store contract rules, after which ground rent is charged)

question: If rejected material is not lifted by the vendor beyond the stipulated period, Railways may charge:

options.A: Ground Rent / Storage Charges (and eventually auction the material as per conditions)

question: What is 'Warranty Guarantee (BG)' clause in store purchase contracts?

options.A: Requirement for supplier to provide Bank Guarantee ensuring rectification/replacement if item fails during warranty period

question: What happens when a component fails within its warranty period on a Metro coach on shop floor?

options.A: Shop issues a Warranty Rejection Advice to Stores/Vendor for free replacement/repair
options.B: Shop buys a new item from employee's personal salary

question: What is 'Earnest Money Deposit' (EMD) submitted by bidders in store tenders?

options.A: Monetary deposit submitted along with tender to establish bidder's earnestness and sincerity to participate

question: What is 'Security Deposit' (SD) submitted by a successful supplier?

options.A: Financial security deposited after contract award to guarantee due performance and fulfillment of contract conditions

question: What is 'Limited Tender' in store procurement?

options.A: Tender invitation issued directly to a limited number of registered/approved suppliers on the approved vendor list
options.B: Tender published in all international newspapers globally
options.C: Tender given to one local shopkeeper verbally

question: What is 'Open Tender'?

options.A: Procurement notice published publicly on IREPS/GeM where any eligible supplier can participate
options.D: Tender reserved for railway staff only

question: What is 'Single Tender'?

options.A: Tender invitation issued to only one specific firm (used under PAC or extreme emergency conditions)
options.C: Tender submitted by single unmarried person

question: What is 'Global Tender'?

options.A: Tender advertised internationally when required high-tech material is not adequately available from domestic manufacturers

question: Which authority approves the 'Approved List of Vendors' (Vendor Directory) for critical railway components?

options.A: RDSO / CLW / ICF / BLW / Centralized Nodal Agencies

question: What is 'Developmental Vendor' status in Railway vendor classification?

options.A: A vendor approved for placing educational/trial orders to develop technical capability and capacity
options.B: A vendor who builds residential houses
options.C: A vendor who has closed business

question: What is 'Regular Vendor' (Approved Source) status?

options.A: A vendor proven for bulk supply orders after successfully meeting developmental criteria and quality standards

question: What is 'Stock Verification' in Stores Depots and User Wards?

options.A: Physical stock count conducted by independent Accounts Stock Verifiers to reconcile physical stock with ledger balances

question: How frequently are 'A Category' stock items physically verified by Stock Verifiers?

options.A: Once every 6 months (or annually as per store verification rules)

question: How frequently are 'C Category' stock items physically verified?

options.A: Once in two years (or as per prescribed periodic cycle)

question: What document is issued by the Stock Verifier when physical stock is LESS than book ledger balance?

options.A: Stock Sheet (showing shortage)

question: What document is issued when physical stock is MORE than book balance?

options.A: Stock Sheet (showing surplus)

question: Who must explain the cause of stock shortages reported in an Accounts Stock Sheet?

options.A: The Store Keeper / Custodian SSE holding charge of the ward/imprest

question: What is 'Survey Committee' in Railway Workshops?

options.A: Committee of officers appointed to inspect unserviceable stores/machinery and recommend condemnation or write-off

question: Which document is processed by the Survey Committee for condemning assets?

options.A: Survey Report (Form S-2269)

question: What is 'Scrap Lot' in stores scrap depot?

options.A: Accumulated scrap material grouped into a specific lot number by weight/category for public auction

question: Which method is primarily used for selling railway scrap through IREPS online portal?

options.A: e-Auction

question: What is 'Delivery Order' (Form S-2339) issued after scrap auction?

options.A: Document authorizing the successful auction purchaser to lift specified scrap lot quantity from depot within fixed period

question: What is 'Risk Purchase' clause in railway store contracts?

options.A: Right of Railways to purchase material from alternative source at supplier's risk and cost if supplier defaults in supply

question: What are 'Liquidated Damages' (LD) charged to a defaulting supplier?

options.A: Pre-estimated penalty compensation charged for delay in supply of material beyond contract delivery date

question: Standard maximum cap on Liquidated Damages (LD) for delayed supply in standard Railway contracts is generally:

options.A: 10% of total contract value

question: What is 'Option Clause' in major railway store contracts?

options.A: Purchaser's right to increase or decrease the ordered quantity by a specified percentage (e.g., ± 30%) during contract currency
options.B: Option to cancel contract without notice
options.D: Option to pay in foreign currency

question: What is 'Price Variation Clause' (PVC) in long-term store contracts?

options.A: Formula-based adjustment of contract price to account for fluctuations in raw material/labor market indices during contract period
options.B: Fixing price permanently regardless of market

question: What is 'Firm Price Contract'?

options.A: Contract where price remains fixed throughout delivery period without any Price Variation Clause adjustment
options.B: Contract signed by firm owner only
options.C: Contract for building firm boundary wall

question: In store indenting, what does 'Specification' define?

options.A: Detailed technical parameters, drawings, material composition, and testing requirements of required item

question: What is 'IS Specification'?

options.A: Indian Standard Specification established by Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS)

question: What is 'IRS Specification'?

options.A: Indian Railway Standard Specification

question: What does 'OEM' stand for in non-stock equipment spare procurement?

options.A: Original Equipment Manufacturer

question: When buying spare parts for specialized imported Metro equipment, indents are usually placed on OEM under:

options.A: PAC / Single Tender basis
options.B: Open global bidding to local scrap dealers

question: What is 'Stock Card' (or Ledger Sheet) maintained in Stores Depot?

options.A: Official accounting register/card recording every receipt, issue, and progressive balance of a stock item

question: What is 'Out-of-Stock' situation in stores management?

options.A: Condition when physical stock balance of an essential item drops to ZERO, leading to stockout
options.B: Condition when store warehouse is full
options.C: Condition when store is closed on Sunday

question: Out-of-stock situation of Vital items directly leads to:

options.A: Loss of production / Train detentions / Maintenance bottlenecks

question: What is 'Turnover Ratio' (TOR) of Stores inventory?

options.A: (Total Value of Inventory at end of year / Total Value of Issues during the year) × 100

question: A LOWER Stores Turnover Ratio (TOR) percentage indicates:

options.A: Better and more efficient inventory management (less capital locked in unused stock)

question: Target Stores Turnover Ratio (TOR) set by Railway Board for major zonal railways/production units is generally around:

options.A: 10% to 15% (or as periodically revised by Railway Board)

question: What is 'Inactive Stock'?

options.A: Stock items that have not been issued/consumed for more than 12 months but less than 24 months
options.B: Stock items actively issued every hour

question: What action is taken by Stores & User Department regarding 'Surplus / Inactive Stock'?

options.A: Review by Standing Surplus Committee for potential transfer to other depots/railways or write-off

question: What is 'Depot Code' in store accounting?

options.A: Unique 2 or 3 digit numerical code identifying a specific Stores Depot ward location

question: What is 'Sub-Indent'?

options.A: An internal subsidiary indent placed by a shop floor section to its main Shop Imprest / Tool Room ward

question: Which document is processed when a user shop requests urgent issue of stock item out-of-turn to prevent line blockade?

options.A: Urgent / Out-of-turn Stores Requisition duly marked 'EMERGENCY' with supervisory justification

question: What is 'Direct Issue' of stores?

options.A: Material procured against a non-stock indent that is directly delivered and charged to the end-user work order upon receipt
options.B: Material stored in depot ward for 10 years

question: What is 'Capital Stores'?

options.A: Stores materials procured specifically for capital works, new construction projects, or track doubling
options.B: Stores located in national capital Delhi

question: What is 'Revenue Stores'?

options.A: Stores materials procured for routine repair, maintenance, and operation of railway assets
options.B: Stores used to collect passenger ticket revenue

question: Which register is processed by the Store Keeper to record daily receipts and issues of materials in user ward?

options.A: Ward Material Register / Stock Register

question: What is the primary role of 'Integrated Material Management Information System' (iMMIS) on shop floor?

options.A: Complete digital workflow for placing non-stock indents, checking stock availability, issuing materials, and tracking status online

question: Why is proper store indenting and inventory control critical for Metro Railway Kolkata JE/SSE supervisory staff?

options.A: Ensures uninterrupted availability of critical maintenance spares, prevents overstocking/wastage, and maintains train safety & punctuality
options.B: To increase paper filing work in office
